correctness.rationale: Reconstructed stable-set convex hull as join of cycle stable-set polytope and clique singleton vertices, yielding N nonnegative facets, m lifted edge-clique facets and one lifted cycle rank facet. Each lifts a true facet by affine independence. Radius upper bounds follow c_j>=r and normal lengths sqrt(t+2),sqrt(m+a^2t); uniform c=r1 attains min. Active all-positive row(s) force each center coordinate to r, proving uniqueness. Difference F_a(t)=a sqrt(t+2)-sqrt(a^2t+2a+1) strictly decreases; F=1 solves t=a^2-2a-1. Independent numerical contact computations: (a,t)=(2,1) only odd-hole; (3,1) edge, (3,2) both with radius 1/6, (3,3) odd; (4,7) both with radius 1/12. Direct small cases do not establish arbitrary facets.

evidence: The full h-perfect theorem gives r=1/(omega+sqrt omega) when omega>=3, but the joined odd cycle is not h-perfect: its lifted inequality sum x_i+a sum y_j<=a is not an ordinary cycle inequality. For (a,t)=(2,1), true radius 1/5, while h-perfect clique formula 1/(3+sqrt 3)>1/5.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Stronger h-perfect theorem is specifically inapplicable, so cannot dominate the present contact transition. 1-wheel literature describes inequalities/extended formulations but not Euclidean ball tangency.
